This study evaluated the demographic, operative, and early postoperative characteristics of patients undergoing MICS-CABG, off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (OP-CABG) at a single institution.

title: Microbiological aetiology of paediatric ventilator-associated pneumonia and risk factors for carbapenem-resistant acinetobacter and Pseudomonas in a tertiary-care hospital in Thailand
creator: Nicharee Chruakanchana, Napaporn Chantasrisawad, Wirada Horapong, Suvaporn Anugulruengkitt
description: SummaryBackgroundPaediatric ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) worsens outcomes and mortality. Characterizing local microbiology and resistance patterns is crucial for empirical therapy and guiding targeted infection prevention and control.ObjectiveThis study aimed to determine the aetiology of VAP, identify risk factors associated with VAP caused by carbapenem-resistant (CR) Acinetobacter and Pseudomonas, and assess the clinical burden and outcomes of VAP in paediatric patients.

title: Associations between the Planetary Health Diet in Late Pregnancy and Pregnancy Outcomes in Women with a Raised BMI: Insights from the PEARS Study
creator: Aoife Davis, Sophie Callanan, Gillian A Corbett, Eileen C O’Brien, Alexander P Douglass, Fionnuala M McAuliffe
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundDiet quality in pregnancy is a modifiable factor with important implications for maternal and neonatal outcomes. The Planetary Health Diet (PHD), designed to promote both human health and environmental sustainability, has not been comprehensively evaluated in high-risk obstetric populations.ObjectivesThis study aimed to examine the PHD in a pregnant cohort with a raised body mass index (BMI) and its associations with pregnancy outcomes, hypothesizing that greater adherence is associated with more favorable pregnancy outcomes.MethodsThis was a secondary analysis of data from the pregnancy

title: Mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome 12B: role of photon-counting computed tomography in detection of cardiac involvement—a case report
creator: Zixian Chen, Yinjia Wang, Wei Tian, Zhuoli Zhang, Gang Wang, Christoph Jensen, Moisés Jiménez Santos, Ana Devesa, Cemil Izgi, Deepti Ranganathan
description: BackgroundMitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome 12B (MDS12B) is an ultra-rare autosomal recessive disorder caused by SLC25A4 mutations, which encode the mitochondrial adenine nucleotide translocator. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is the predominant manifestation, yet detailed cardiac tissue characterization remains limited.Case summaryA 28-year-old male presented with a 17-year history of exertional palpitations and progressive fatigue.

title: Environmental contamination with canine soil-transmitted helminths in New Zealand urban areas: A nationwide molecular, spatial, and risk factor analysis survey
creator: Madisson Nam, Patsy A. Zendejas-Heredia, Sara Ashby, Sze-Fui Hii, Ushani Atapattu, Lucas Huggins, Anke Wiethoelter, Carl Eden, Maureen Forsyth, Frédéric Beugnet, Neil D. Young, Robin B. Gasser, Rebecca Traub, Vito Colella
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Urban parks and recreational areas are frequent gathering sites for dogs and their owners, where dog waste creates sources for pathogens of veterinary and zoonotic concern. Canine soil-transmitted helminths (cSTHs) such as hookworms (Ancylostoma spp. and Uncinaria stenocephala), roundworms (Toxocara canis and Toxascaris leonina), whipworms (Trichuris vulpis), and threadworms (Strongyloides stercoralis), are recognised for their ability to cause gastrointestinal disease and other health issues in dogs. In addition, some species are known for being zoonotic and cause potentially life-threatening conditions in humans.

title: Intersectional inequalities in COVID-19 hospitalisation and mortality: A nationwide MAIHDA study of Swedish adults across four pandemic waves (2020–2022)
creator: Jesper Löve, Gunilla Priebe, Bo Burström, Ailiana Santosa, Nawi Ng
description: BackgroundCOVID-19 has been described as a syndemic shaped by interactions between viral exposure, co-morbidities, and social inequalities. However, much of the literature relies on single-axis analyses and restricted time horizons, obscuring how health inequalities shifted across pandemic phases. Intersectionality theory conceptualises how social positions intersect within systems of power to produce context-dependent inequalities.

title: Novel ternary covalent complexes (OsrhLF-EGCG-Mal) based on plant-derived recombinant lactoferrin (OsrhLF) by polyphenol-carbohydrate dual-modification strategy
creator: Xueya Li, Xiaoyan Guan, Yeting Wu, Wanrong Wu, Yingying Li, Rui Liu, Zixian Xia, Yifeng Ding, Yanchun Shao, Youyou Lu
description: Bovine lactoferrin was widely used in food industry but suffered from resource dependence, environmental sensitivity and digestive inactivation susceptibility. As a promising alternative, the characteristics of plant-derived recombinant lactoferrin (OsrhLF) remained unclear. Herein, novel OsrhLF-EGCG-Mal ternary covalent complexes were innovatively constructed via dual-modification strategy with epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) and maltodextrin (Mal).

title: Hybridization chain reaction-based aptasensor for sensitive detection of Staphylococcus aureus in milk
creator: Xiaoli Wu, Qun Zhao, Yingying Wang, Lijun Liu, Alideertu Dong, Cong Wang, Yuchun Guo, Haixia Wu
description: Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) is recognized as a high-risk pathogen responsible for severe food safety incidents. To address this concern, this study developed a fluorescent aptasensor based on fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) for the rapid detection of S. aureus in milk. The proposed strategy employed high-specificity aptamers as recognition elements.

title: Chitosan/Carboxymethyl cellulose edible coating loaded with aggregation-induced emission photosensitizers: A robust yet biocompatible antimicrobial film for Litchi preservation
creator: Shuiyuan Liang, Jiahui Guo, Xiyu Jiao, Hongtao Lei, Tian Guan
description: Litchi deteriorates rapidly postharvest due to high moisture, enzymatic browning, and microbes. In this work, an eco-friendly, antimicrobial aggregation-induced emission photosensitizers-loaded chitosan/carboxymethyl cellulose (AIE-CS/CMC) coating film was developed and validated to significantly delayed pericarp browning, inhibited spoilage and retained most of the nutrients, extending litchi's shelf life by approximately eight days compared with the untreated water-blank control.

title: Reply to "Comment on 'K-Alpha calculator, Krippendorff's Alpha calculator: A user-friendly tool for computing Krippendorff's Alpha inter-rater reliability coefficient': Reconciling the ratio-scale computational implementation"
creator: Giacomo Marzi, Marco Balzano, Davide Marchiori
description: a calculator: A user-friendly tool for computing Krippendorff's Alpha inter-rater reliability coefficient': Reconciling the ratio-scale computational implementation" published in MethodsX). The issue is confined to a specific part of the ratio-scale computation, while the nominal, ordinal, and interval computations are unaffected and require no change. Ratio-scale computations on datasets whose minimum value is 1 are likewise unaffected.

title: Comment on “a novel parameter for risk stratification in patients with Takotsubo syndrome”
creator: Güney Sarıoğlu, Yakup Yiğit
description: asingly recognized as involving systemic inflammatory responses. An important interpretative issue, however, is whether FAR should be considered a distinct prognostic biomarker or primarily a composite expression of its two components. Fibrinogen and albumin respond in opposite directions during systemic inflammation, and albumin may also reflect nutritional status, vascular permeability, hepatic synthesis, and overall illness burden.

title: Astrocyte-centered temporal resilience at the brain–behavior–immunity interface: sleep–circadian disruption and perioperative cognitive vulnerability in older adults
creator: Wei Fan, Shuai Han, Cunjing Wang, Ju Gao
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Perioperative cognitive vulnerability in older adults reflects interactions among inflammatory stress, altered brain state, sleep–circadian disruption, and recovery capacity. This narrative review examines astrocyte-centered temporal resilience as a hypothesis-generating framework for integrating these brain–immune–behavior processes. Astrocytes participate in sleep-pressure signaling, circadian regulation, neurometabolic support, inflammatory responses, extracellular homeostasis, and clearance-related physiology; however, these functions operate within broader neuronal, microglial, vascular, endocrine, and environmental networks.

title: Genomic insights into carbapenemase- and extended-spectrum β-lactamase–producing gram-negative bacteria in aquatic and terrestrial animal reservoirs in the United Arab Emirates
creator: Hazim O Khalifa, Temesgen Mohammed, Hazem Ramadan, Afra Abdalla, Ann Mary Joseph, Natassia Mannina, Uday Kishore, Arve Lee Willingham
description: BackgroundThe global spread of carbapenemase- and extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL)–producing Gram-negative bacteria represents a major One Health challenge, driven by interconnected human, animal, and environmental reservoirs. However, genomic data on antimicrobial-resistant bacteria associated with aquatic and terrestrial animals in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) remain scarce, limiting assessment of their potential role in resistance dissemination.

title: Allergic Contact Dermatitis to 2-Octyl Cyanoacrylate After Total Joint Arthroplasty: A Single-Surgeon Case Series
creator: Stefano Ghirardelli, Ittai Shichman, Mohammed El-Hassan, PierFrancesco Indelli, Peter K. Sculco
description: Background2-Octyl cyanoacrylate is widely used for surgical skin closure in orthopaedic procedures, offering advantages such as ease of application, strong adherence, and favorable cosmetic outcomes. However, allergic contact dermatitis (ACD) is a rare yet recognized complication resulting in topical and systemic treatments and a theoretical risk for superficial and deep periprosthetic joint infection (PJI).

title: Quantitative refinement and multicentre psychometric validation of the Chinese total knee arthroplasty patient-reported outcome measure: a prospective cohort study with repeated measures
creator: Chao Xu, Xiaofeng Chang, Feng Ye, Haodong Wu, Guo Chen, Rui Zhang, Shuxin Yao, Lei Shang, Jianbing Ma
description: SummaryBackgroundTotal knee arthroplasty (TKA) requires valid, culturally appropriate patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs). A 35-item preliminary Chinese Total Knee Arthroplasty Patient-reported Outcome Measurement (CTP) was previously developed by our group through qualitative research with Chinese patients and multidisciplinary experts, but it had not undergone quantitative refinement or prospective multicentre psychometric validation.

title: Rimegepant for vestibular and cochlear symptoms associated with vertigo in a real-world retrospective study
creator: Ziyu Zhai, E Tian, Wandi Xu, Jun Wang, Zhaoqi Guo, Jingyu Chen, Zhanghong Zhou, Xixi Yu, Ni Zhai, Shun Zhou, Xinbo Gao, Xin Zhang, Yisheng Lu, Yixu Wang, Xin Ma, Sulin Zhang
description: SummaryVertigo commonly co-occurs with cochlear symptoms, yet evidence for calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) receptor antagonists across audiovestibular disorders remains limited. We retrospectively evaluated 54 adults with vertigo who received rimegepant 75 mg daily or every other day for 8 weeks.

title: Anti-N-methyl-d-aspartate (NMDA) receptor encephalitis associated with mature ovarian teratoma: a case report
creator: Aaron Adams, Elizabeth Farabee, Chelsae Nugent, Whitney Goldsberry
description: Anti-N-methyl-d-aspartate (NMDA) receptor encephalitis is an autoimmune condition often characterized by acute neuropsychiatric manifestations, including psychiatric symptoms, seizures, autonomic instability, and cognitive dysfunction. Early diagnosis and treatment are crucial for improving patient outcomes.This report presents the case of a 27-year-old woman with known anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis who experienced progressive worsening of confusion, memory loss, and agitation.

title: A coronary event without coronary artery disease: the hidden role of inherited thrombophilia—a case report
creator: Nika Kuridze, Revaz Sturua, Levan Tsaguria
description: BackgroundST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) in young patients without traditional cardiovascular risk factors requires evaluation beyond atherosclerotic disease. Inherited thrombophilia and cancer-related prothrombotic states represent important alternative aetiologies.Case summaryA 42-year-old man presented with an acute inferior STEMI. Coronary angiography demonstrated thrombotic occlusion of the proximal right coronary artery, treated with drug-eluting stent implantation. The patient had no cardiovascular risk factors.

title: Assessment of preload responsiveness by variation in peak aortic flow velocity in suprasternal window: A novel approach
creator: Jasnoor Kaur, Ajay Kumar, Mayank Priyadarshi, Anshuman Darbari
description: measurement have been found to be 14% and 11%, respectively.[23] These variabilities are similar to the fluid responsiveness thresholds of 10% and 15% used commonly, which may result in inadvertent fluid administration. A study, assessing aortic valve status in patients with aortic stenosis, found the aortic peak velocity to have less measurement error (3.2%) compared to LVOT-VTI (22%).

title: Pulmonary venous baffle stenosis following atrial switch repair for transposition of the great arteries
creator: Sri Rama Ananta Nagabhushanam Padala, Aaditya Sirohi, Prathamesh G. Kumbhar, Anjali Tiwari
description: ents with late presentation, particularly in developing countries.[2] With increasing long-term survivors, delayed complications, including systemic right ventricular dysfunction and baffle-related obstruction, are increasingly encountered. Here, we report a case of pulmonary venous baffle (PVB) stenosis that presented 7 years after Senning’s operation.

title: Sleep duration and quality among Indian anaesthesiologists: A nationwide cross-sectional survey
creator: Kapil Singhal, Kritika Agrawal, Deepak Thapa
description: Background and Aims:Poor sleep can adversely affect well-being, cognitive function, and decision-making. Anaesthesiologists face unique occupational challenges (irregular shifts, on-call duties, and high stress), which exacerbate sleep disturbances. This study aimed to assess the prevalence of poor sleep among Indian anaesthesiologists and identify associated risk factors.Methods:A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among Indian anaesthesiologists.

title: Tracking the tip: Preventing the malposition of central venous catheters
creator: Bhavya Naithani, Rudrashish Haldar, Soumya Sankar Nath
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). contribute to operator complacency, particularly when correct catheter position is inferred solely from the ability to aspirate dark venous blood from a functioning lumen. The assumption that successful venous cannulation equates to correct catheter placement is therefore misleading.

title: Case report: aortic root thrombus presenting with syncope and embolic events
creator: Ai Phi Thuy Ho, Eirik Brekka Tjønnfjord, Ole-Christian Walter Rutherford, Josip Andelo Borovac, Thierry Carrel, Guillermo Careaga-Reyna, Deepti Ranganathan
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAortic root thrombus is a rare but potentially life-threatening condition, often associated with systemic embolization or obstruction of coronary arteries (myocardial infarction). The most common reason is a complication of left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation, but it may occur in the absence of LVAD, for instance in structural valve disease or prothrombotic disorders (antiphospholipid syndrome, haemolytic diseases, and myeloproliferative disease, making diagnosis challenging.Case summaryWe report the case of a 47-year-old man with a history of deep venous thrombosis who presented with

title: Sustainable Hierarchical Networking for Extreme-Edge AI-Based Wildlife Monitoring in Resource-Constrained Environments
creator: Md Auhidur Rahman, Ervisa Marku, Sunil Mathew, Davide Adami, Michele Pagano, Stefano Giordano
description: Deploying artificial intelligence (AI) for wildlife monitoring in remote environments remains challenging due to limited energy, computational resources, and unreliable communication. Conventional edge AI systems rely on continuous sensing, high-power communication, and full-precision models, resulting in excessive energy consumption. This paper presents a green-energy-based hierarchical network architecture for sustainable wildlife monitoring at the extreme edge.

title: Feature-PLPD-Aided Visual–Inertial Odometry for Low-Cost Embedded Systems
creator: Ayoub Mamri, Abdelhafid El Hadri, Abdelaziz Benallegue, Khalil Hachicha
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Visual–Inertial Odometry (VIO) has become a key technology for motion estimation in robotics and autonomous systems. However, deploying accurate VIO pipelines on embedded platforms remains challenging due to the trade-off between estimation accuracy, real-time performance, and energy consumption. This paper presents a hardware-aware Feature-PLPD VIO framework that integrates a point-and-line visual front-end with a loosely coupled Error-State Extended Kalman Filter (ESEKF) back-end. The proposed approach follows Algorithm Architecture Adequacy (A3) principles to preserve estimation robustness while limiting computational and memory requirements.

title: Sensor-Based Dynamic Response and Stress Estimation in Monolithic and Laminated Glass Beams Under Soft Impact Loading
creator: Natalia García-Fernández, F. Pelayo, Manuel Aenlle, Mario López-Gallego, María Jesús Lamela-Rey
description: Monolithic and laminated glass elements are increasingly used in structural applications, where their response to impact loading must be assessed to ensure safety. For soft impacts, simplified simulations based only on the initial impact velocity may be inaccurate because the transient coupling between the impactor and the glass depends on the impactor stiffness and mass.

title: Adaptive Kernel Density Soft-Gating for Robust GNSS/INS Georeferencing of Highly Dynamic Remote-Sensing Platforms Under Measurement Outliers
creator: Kaiqiang Feng, Jie Li, Zhirui Sun
description: GNSS measurement outliers degrade positioning accuracy in integrated global navigation satellite system/inertial navigation system (GNSS/INS) georeferencing for highly dynamic remote-sensing platforms. This study presents an adaptive kernel density robust Kalman filter (KDE-RKF) for attenuating anomalous observations through continuous measurement weighting.

title: Design, Synthesis and Antihyperglycemic/Antilipidemic Activities of Quinoline-thiazolidine-2,4-dione Hybrid
creator: ElShimaa Ahmed Mohamed Abousaada, Asmaa Galal-Khallaf, Khaled Mohammed-Geba, Mohamed El-Bahnsawye, Mona K. Abo Hussein, Elshaymaa I. Elmongy, Rania Ali Ahmed Shaltout, Reem Binsuwaidan, Hadeer Ali, Ahmed I. El-Tantawy, Hamed Abdel-Bary, Ibrahim El Tantawy El Sayed
description: Background: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and hyperlipidemia are interrelated metabolic disorders that significantly increase cardiovascular risk. Thiazolidinediones are known insulin sensitizers, whereas quinoline derivatives possess diverse pharmacological activities. To explore their complementary activity, we designed a novel hybrid compound integrating a thiazolidinedione core with a quinoline moiety via a carbon spacer.

title: Fabrication of a Flexible PDMS/MWCNTs Composite Sensor Based on a Triboelectric Nanogenerator (Teng) and Its Application in Pulse Monitoring
creator: Longfei Zhang, Guowei Gao
description: In view of the demand for wearable physiological monitoring, porous PDMS/MWCNTs composite films were fabricated via the sacrificial template method in this work. Output performance tests were carried out on films with different sacrificial particle sizes, film thicknesses, and multi-walled carbon nanotube (MWCNT) mass fractions. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) was employed for structural morphology characterization.

title: Comparative Evaluation of CNN and Transformer-Based Instance Segmentation Architectures for Whitefly Detection in Citrus Crops
creator: Luis Manzano-Soto, Christian Fernández-Campusano, Humberto Verdejo-Fredes, Cristhian Becker, Raúl Carrasco
description: This study focuses on the detection of pests in citrus fruits using computer vision (CV) techniques and image detection technologies based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Early detection enables pest control, reduces the use of pesticides, and generates alerts for the inspection of surrounding areas.

title: Coupling Hydrological Scenarios and Water Footprints for Multi-Objective Cropping-Structure Optimization in the Middle and Lower Shiyang River Basin
creator: Yuhong Pu, Guangping Qi, Yubin Zhang, Yanxia Kang, Yayu Wang, Zhongxia Tang, Haohao Dang, Fusen Yang, Demin Fu
description: Hydrological fluctuations affect cropping-structure optimization in arid inland river basins by altering agricultural water-supply boundaries and crop yields. This study focused on five counties and districts in the middle and lower reaches of the Shiyang River Basin. Based on the 1995–2024 runoff series, four hydrological scenarios—wet, normal, dry, and extremely dry—were constructed.

title: Clinical Outcomes According to Age and Atrial Fibrillation Type: Insights from the Multicentre REGUEIFA Registry
creator: Alejandro Manuel López-Pena, Juliana Elices-Teja, Olga Durán-Bobín, Laila González-Melchor, María Vázquez-Caamaño, Emiliano Fernández-Obanza, Eva González-Babarro, Pilar Cabanas-Grandío, Miriam Piñeiro-Portela, Oscar Prada-Delgado, Mario Gutiérrez-Feijoo, Evaristo Freire, Oscar Díaz-Castro, Javier M
description: Background/Objectives: Atrial fibrillation (AF) represents the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia, and its incidence rises markedly with advancing age. The relative prognostic impact of age compared with AF type remains uncertain. This study assessed the association between age, AF type, and clinical outcomes in a large real-world AF cohort.

title: Comparative Effectiveness of Amiodarone Versus Lidocaine as Antiarrhythmic Therapy for Cardiac Arrest with Shockable Rhythms: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
creator: Faizan Ahmed, Ayesha Zulfiqar, Tooba Nihal, Maliha Khalid, M Rafiqul Islam, Fnu Abubakar, Noor ul Ain Saleem, Haris Bin Tahir, Hafsa Arshad Azam Raja, Areej Dar, Omar Kamel, Faseeh Haider, Saman Rauf, Wania Ayub, Khush Dadhania, Mobeen Zaka Haider, Yasar Sattar, Amro Taha
description: Background: Amiodarone and lidocaine are antiarrhythmic agents recommended for advanced cardiac life support in shockable ventricular arrhythmias during cardiac arrest, yet their comparative effectiveness in in-hospital (IHCA) and out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) remains uncertain. Methods: From 930 records identified in PubMed, ScienceDirect, Embase, and Cochrane Library, 14 studies were included.

title: Multidimensional Physiological and Gut Microbiome Profiling Identifies Subtle Physiological Patterns in an Apparently Healthy Aging Indian Cohort: A Cross-Sectional Observational Study
creator: Gangaraju Divyashri, Harini Hutti, Lalitha Prasanna Madduri Venkata, Bipin Pradeep Kumar, Ayako Yachie, Samik Ghosh
description: Aging is characterized by gradual shifts in cellular and physiological processes, even in individuals who remain apparently clinically healthy. These changes reflect a coordinated decline in metabolic efficiency, immune regulation, organ function, psychological resilience, and sleep integrity, domains increasingly recognized as interconnected determinants of apparently healthy aging.

title: Effect of Nb Microalloying on the Dynamic Recrystallization, Bainitic Microstructure, and Mechanical Properties of Hot-Rolled Bainitic Steels
creator: Rui Cao, Shangqing Chen, Junheng Gao, Haitao Zhao, Qingxiao Feng, Honghui Wu, Chaolei Zhang, Yuhe Huang, Jun Lu, Shuize Wang, Xinping Mao
description: Controlling prior austenite morphology during single-pass hot rolling is essential for improving the strength–ductility balance of strip casting high-strength steels. In this study, Fe–0.24C–1.5Si–1.8Mn steels with and without 0.03 wt.% Nb were deformed by 50% at 950–1100 °C and subsequently held at 350 °C for 60 min for bainitic transformation.

title: Stress Field Prediction and DIC-Informed Spatial Regularization for AlSi10Mg Alloy Tensile Specimens Based on Graph Neural Networks
creator: Zhongying Dong, Xingbo Xie, Guili Yang, Zhangdong Li, Xinghua Li, Huayuan Ma
description: HighlightsFiLM-GNN predicts von Mises stress with R2 = 0.9984 and RMSE = 4.60 MPa.The independent force branch reconstructs dense curves with R2 = 0.9957.DIC-informed spatial regularization improves DIC spatial shape loss by 3.21% with 0.232 MPa mean correction.The framework enables rapid full-field prediction with conservative experiment-informed spatial regularization.Field–force decoupling enables curve-specific tuning without altering spatial fields.

title: Clinical Significance of Tumor Infiltrating Lymphocytes and Modulation by Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy in Colorectal Cancer Liver Metastases
creator: Yasaman Rezaie, Kerryan Ashley, Janie Zhang, Thejal Srikumar, Jassim DiPalermo, Kurt A. Schalper, Michael Cecchini
description: Simple SummaryColorectal cancer frequently spreads to the liver, where tumors resist immunotherapy through poorly understood mechanisms. Using quantitative multiplexed immunofluorescence in two independent patient cohorts, we measured CD4+, CD8+, and FOXP3+ regulatory T-cells in matched primary tumors and liver metastases.

title: Prenatal humid heat exposure and cord blood extracellular vesicle microRNA profiles in a Ghanaian Pregnancy Cohort: GRAPHS
creator: Alison Lee, Seyram Kaali, Michelle Li, Mohammed Mujtaba Nuhu, Elena Colicino, Musah Osei, Darby Jack, Sule Awuni, Steven N Chillrud, Haotian Wu, Abigail Gaylord, Cascade Tuholske, Kwaku Poku Asante
description: Humid heat exposures over pregnancy impact birth outcomes but mechanisms are poorly described. We leveraged the Ghana Randomized Air Pollution and Health Study (GRAPHS) to examine associations between maximum shaded wet bulb globe temperature (WBGT) and cord blood extracellular vesicle (EV)-associated microRNA. We also considered heat index (HI) and dry air temperature as secondary exposures.

title: Chronic Stress and the Brain–Kidney Axis in Renal Injury: From Neuroendocrine Dysregulation to Kidney Damage
creator: Chunyun Zhang, Cheng Wan, Jing Sun, Zhiwen Wang, Qian Yuan, Chun Zhang
description: Chronic stress is a pervasive psychophysiological burden and an independent risk factor for chronic kidney disease (CKD). Large-scale cohort studies confirm that stress exposure significantly increases CKD risk and accelerates renal decline, even after adjusting for traditional confounders. However, the neuroendocrine mechanisms translating stress into direct kidney damage remain unclear.

title: BPC 157 in Rodent Ischemia–Reperfusion Injury: A Critical Review of Preclinical Evidence
creator: Hüseyin Demirtaş
description: Ischemia–reperfusion injury (IRI) is a clinically important consequence of blood-flow restoration after ischemia and contributes to tissue damage across multiple organ systems. This critical review evaluates the preclinical evidence for BPC 157 in rodent IRI and related reperfusion-associated vascular injury models, with particular attention to oxidative stress, endothelial and nitric oxide (NO)-related responses, inflammation, apoptosis, angiogenic signaling, and tissue injury.

title: Comparative Study on Taste and Odor Flavor Compounds of Chrysanthemums from Five Different Varieties Using UPLC-Q-TOF-MS, GC-MS, E-Tongue, E-Nose, and Chemometrics
creator: Guizhou Hu, Xinqi Li, Geng Qin, Ailing Ben, Jin Qi
description: A practical strategy was established for distinguishing five varieties of Chrysanthemums by combining E-tongue, E-nose, GC-MS, and LC-Q-TOF-MS. A total of 19 low molecule fraction compounds and 26 volatile fraction compounds were identified as the common peaks. Chemometrics were used to screen the characteristic compounds of the five varieties of Chrysanthemums.

title: Orbital Defect Size Reflects Structural Displacement but Not Ocular Motor Dysfunction: A Cohort Study of 1084 Patients
creator: Tal Capucha, Ahmad Hija, Chaim Ohayon, Andrei Krasovsky, Amir Wolff, Omri Emodi
description: Background/Objectives: Orbital defect size is widely used as a surrogate for fracture severity, yet a larger bony opening and direct injury to the extraocular apparatus are not the same. We tested whether defect magnitude provides comparable information about structural displacement and ocular motor dysfunction. Methods: Retrospective cohort of CT-confirmed orbital fractures at a level 1 trauma center, 2001–2023.

title: Hygiene Knowledge and Digital Health Literacy in Emergency Medical Services in Germany: A Cross-Sectional Study of EMS Personnel and Emergency Physicians with Relevance for the Development of Training Programmes
creator: Veit Kinne, Dragisa Mitic, Nora Helke Leder, Sebastian Lang, Kristin Büchel, Frank Kipp, Sabine Trommer
description: Highlights What are the main findings? WHO-based hand hygiene knowledge among EMS personnel and emergency physicians was generally moderate to good, whereas the extended hygiene knowledge test on basic hygiene measures, PPE use, and MDRO management indicated knowledge gaps in additional areas.

title: Effect of Nursing Intervention Supported by Mobile Health Applications on Asthma Control, Maternal and Neonatal Outcomes Among Pregnant Women with Asthma
creator: Hanan E. Nada, Ishraga Abdelgadir Ibrahim Mohamed, Faten Shawky Kandil, Hanan G. El-Bready, Fatma Ahmed Elsobkey, Safaa Gaber Aly Salem, Marwa A. Shahin, Enas Mohamed Lotfy
description: Background: Asthma during pregnancy is associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. Nursing education, self-management support, and mobile health (mHealth) technologies may support asthma management during pregnancy. Aim: This study evaluated the effect of a structured nursing intervention supported by an mHealth application on asthma control, treatment adherence, and self-monitoring, and maternal and neonatal outcomes among pregnant women with asthma.

title: Nonconvulsive and Electrographic Status Epilepticus in Comatose Adult Survivors of Cardiac Arrest: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Prevalence, EEG-Based Diagnosis, Treatment, and Neurological Outcomes
creator: Vivek Gupta, Viswanath Vasudevan
description: Highlights What are the main findings? The pooled prevalence of NCSE/ESE/PSE was 22% among EEG-monitored comatose survivors of cardiac arrest, although prevalence varied substantially across EEG definitions, timing, and monitoring strategies.EEG-defined status epilepticus and related electrographic abnormalities were associated with high rates of poor neurological outcome and death, but recovery was documented in selected patients.

title: Peptidome and Metabolome Profiling of Fermented Milk Products Reveal Accumulation of Bioactive Compounds During Cold Storage
creator: Maxim S. Sheludchenko, Elena V. Kovalenko, Olesya O. Shoshina, Vera E. Odintsova, Stanislav I. Koshechkin, Olesya I. Volokh
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This study assessed the metabolome and peptidome profiles of cow’s milk and four traditional fermented milk products produced using standard sets of starter cultures. Many of these microbe-generated molecules exhibit biological activities that can affect human health. We used non-targeted metabolomic methods to assess semi-quantified concentrations of four types of molecules in the final products: peptides; amino acids; long-, medium-, and short-chain fatty acids; and mono- and disaccharides and their derivatives. Ultra-performance liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS) was performed on the peptidomes.

title: S-Adenosylmethionine-Dependent Methylation, Protein Arginine Methyltransferases and Cardiovascular Diseases
creator: Zi Yan, Wenhui Zhao, Naixin Zhao, Jianguo Li
description: Methylation, catalyzed by a diverse family of S-adenosylmethionine (SAM)-dependent methyltransferases, is a fundamental biochemical process that regulates the function of proteins, DNA, and RNA. Among these modifications, protein arginine methylation, catalyzed by protein arginine methyltransferases (PRMTs), represents a critical post-translational mechanism regulating transcription, DNA repair, RNA splicing, and signal transduction.

title: Type I Interferon Emerges as the Reproducible Core of a Shared Mitochondrial–Immune Transcriptomic Signature in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension and Bipolar Disorder
creator: Cristina Ioana Stoica, Cătălin Araniciu, Ioana Andrada Ionuț, Anca Stana, Smaranda Dafina Oniga
description: Background/Objectives: Mitochondrial dysfunction and immune activation are reported across many chronic diseases, yet whether such shared signals are reproducible across independent cohorts is rarely tested. We compared the peripheral blood transcriptomes of two clinically distinct disorders, pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) and bipolar disorder (BD), to determine which shared transcriptomic signals remain directionally concordant across independent cohorts.

title: Development of Novel Prenatal Prediction Models for Birth-Weight Estimation in Low-Risk Third-Trimester Pregnancies
creator: Sevda Yelec, Rauf Melekoglu, Yusuf Kemal Arslan, Cihan Cetin, Selim Buyukkurt, Gulsah Seydaoglu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Objective: Sonographic evaluation of the fetus and estimation of fetal weight are integral components of modern obstetric practice. Estimated fetal weight (EFW) plays a crucial role in predicting macrosomia, diagnosing intrauterine growth restriction, and monitoring fetal development. This study aimed to improve birth-weight prediction in low-risk term pregnancies by combining conventional fetal biometry with maternal anthropometry and selected fetal soft-tissue and cardiac measurements.

title: Immune and Redox Responses of Galleria mellonella to Caffeic Acid: Concentration- and Time-Dependent Patterns
creator: Fatih Battal, Serhat Kaya
description: Background/Objectives: Caffeic acid is a naturally occurring phenolic compound with antioxidant and immunomodulatory properties, but its integrated effects on innate immune and redox-related physiology in Galleria mellonella remain unclear. This study evaluated concentration- and time-related effects of caffeic acid on immune and biochemical endpoints. Methods: Last-instar larvae were exposed to 0.

title: Study on the Effects of Flow Fields Under the Refuge Effect of Artificial Reefs on the Behavior and Physiology of Juvenile Lutjanus erythopterus
creator: Yu Guo, Dezhong Kong, Changlin Li, Chuanxin Qin, Gang Yu, Zhenhua Ma
description: Simple SummaryHabitat restoration represented by artificial reefs is a vital means of protecting marine fishery resources. Offshore wind turbine foundations resemble artificial reefs in flow disturbance and shelter function, but the combined influence of the flow field and reef shelters on juvenile reef fish is still unclear.

title: Effects of Virtual Pedagogical Agents and Instructional Content Type on Learners’ Experience in Online Learning: Evidence from Behavioral, Eye-Tracking, and EEG Data
creator: Shasha Liu, Xiaoqi Shen, Tiansheng Xia
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Online learning has become an important means of acquiring knowledge. Virtual pedagogical agents have gradually evolved from auxiliary tools into intelligent instructional media capable of affective interaction. However, how these agents affect learning outcomes remains unclear. Integrating social agency theory and cognitive load theory, this study developed a model in which virtual pedagogical agent type was the independent variable; learning experience was the dependent variable; psychological distance, emotional attachment, and attentional engagement were mediators; and instructional content type was the moderator.

title: White Wine Intake Reduces Mitochondrial Complex I-Derived ROS in the Male Rat Heart
creator: Jeronim Matijevic, Marko Grahovac, Marin Mornar, Ivana Novak, Marko Ljubkovic, Mladen Boban, Jasna Marinovic
description: Epidemiological studies suggest that, despite the adverse effects of excessive alcohol intake, low-to-moderate levels of wine consumption have been associated with favorable cardiovascular outcomes. While the biological effects of polyphenol-rich red wine have been extensively studied, less is known about the impact of white wine on myocardial cellular function and the underlying mechanisms.

title: Noninvasive Preoperative Stratification of Renal Tumors for Aggressiveness and Prognosis
creator: Jinglai Lin, Linpeng Yao, Jianbo Gao, Ning Xu, Ying Xiong, Qi Bai, Kang Wang, Qi Sun
description: Accurate preoperative discrimination between indolent and aggressive renal lesions is essential for personalized risk-stratified management and improves the clinical outcomes of renal tumor patients. This study aimed to establish and externally validate a non-invasive computed tomography (CT)-derived radiomic model for identifying aggressive renal tumors and predicting long-term postoperative survival.

title: Effects of Chronic Low-Temperature Exposure on the Behaviour of Adult Zebrafish (Danio rerio)
creator: Amalys Sofia Sanchez Garcia, Flavia Frabetti, Gabriella Tedeschi, Arianna Racca, Enrico Alleva, Mattia Toni
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Simple SummaryTemperature strongly affects how fish behave and function. In this study, adult zebrafish were kept for three weeks at a lower temperature (18 °C) and compared with fish maintained at a more favourable temperature (26 °C). Their behaviour was examined in different situations, including exploration of a novel environment, choice between light and dark zones, interaction with other conspecifics, and response to their own reflection. Fish exposed to cold water moved less, explored less, and spent more time inactive.

title: Experimental warming alleviates leaf-level physiological stress of Kobresia pygmaea in alpine meadows on the Northeastern Qinghai-Tibet Plateau
creator: Lei Zheng, Xiaodong Wu, Genghao Ji, Guimin Liu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundClimate warming can strongly influence alpine plant physiology, but the leaf-level responses of dominant alpine meadow species to warming may vary across elevation and growing-season stages. These spatial and seasonal patterns remain insufficiently known.ResultsWe examined the physiological responses of Kobresia pygmaea on the northeastern Qinghai-Tibet Plateau to long-term passive open-top chamber (OTC) warming across four elevations (3691, 3786, 3981, and 4131 m a.s.l.) from July to September.

title: Enhancing ZnO Efficiency: Humic Substances as Natural Carriers and Stabilizers for ZnO Nanoparticles for Sustainable Agriculture
creator: Tianyi Shen, Gleb N. Trishkin, Maria G. Chernysheva, Natalia A. Kulikova, Ivan V. Mikheev, Grigorii R. Chermashentsev, Sergey V. Maksimov, Gennadii A. Badun
description: Zinc is an essential micronutrient in agricultural systems, fulfilling vital roles in both plant physiology and modern fertilizer formulations. Despite its importance, zinc deficiency has emerged as one of the most prevalent micronutrient limitations in global agriculture. Humic acids (HA) can serve as effective transporters of trace elements for crops, including in foliar fertilization.

title: Perceived Noise Levels in Intensive Care Units and Their Self-Reported Adverse Effects on Nurses in Saudi Arabia: A Cross-Sectional Study
creator: Nabat Almalki, Atheer Asiri, Lama Alkhaldi, Huda Majrashi, Abeer Almotairi, Amal Alfifi, Hind Althobaiti, Badriah Althubaiti, Jawharah Alhufayyan, Bushra Alshammari, Mawahib Almalki
description: Background/Objectives: Intensive care units (ICUs) are acoustically demanding environments in which nurses are continuously exposed to alarms, medical equipment, and staff activity. This study assessed ICU nurses’ perceived internal and external noise levels and their perceived noise-related adverse effects, and examined whether these perceptions differed according to demographic and work-related characteristics.

title: Congenital Clubfoot as an Early Manifestation of Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy?
creator: Vladimir Kenis, Pavel Shpulev, Evgeniya Melnik, Irina Sosnina, Evgeniya Snegova
description: Background: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is the most common X-linked progressive neuromuscular disorder of childhood. The classic course of DMD is characterized by onset after a period of normal motor development. However, in recent years, evidence has been accumulating of prodromal features of the disease, including speech delays and neurocognitive impairments.

title: Effects of Replacing Fish Meal with Poultry By-Product Meal on Growth, Physiological Status, Disease Resistance, and Hepatic Transcriptomic Responses in Hybrid Yellow Catfish (Pelteobagrus fulvidraco ♀ × Pelteobagrus vachelli ♂)
creator: Peng Shi, Lei Wang, Xuxiong Huang, Biao Yun, Xueqiao Qian
description: Purpose: This study evaluated the effects of replacing dietary fish meal (FM) with poultry by-product meal (PBM) on growth, physiological status, disease resistance, and hepatic transcriptomic responses in hybrid yellow catfish (Pelteobagrus fulvidraco ♀ × Pelteobagrus vachelli ♂). Methods: Six isonitrogenous and isolipidic diets were formulated by replacing 0%, 12%, 24%, 36%, 48%, or 60% of dietary FM with PBM.

title: Written Languaging with Direct Feedback in Beginner CSL Writing: A Crossover Study of Metacognitive Engagement and Transfer Effects
creator: Ming Lyu, Baoqian Yang, Wenting He
description: Understanding the cognitive architectures that enable learners to process feedback and self-regulate is fundamental to fostering intelligent second language (L2) learning, particularly as AI-based pedagogies become prevalent. Direct written corrective feedback, while common in beginner L2 writing, often triggers only surface-level processing.

title: Multidimensional Recovery Trajectories Throughout Breast Cancer Treatment and Survivorship: A Prospective Longitudinal Study
creator: Laura Lorenzo-Gallego, Nicola S. Diciolla, Fernando Ramos-Gómez, Virginia Prieto-Gómez, Aldina Couso-González, María Torres-Lacomba
description: Simple SummaryMany women continue to experience physical, sensory, and emotional problems after breast cancer treatment, even when pain levels appear to improve. Understanding how recovery evolves over time is essential to provide appropriate follow-up and support during survivorship. In this prospective longitudinal study, women were assessed before surgery and throughout treatment using clinical, sensory, functional, and quality-of-life measures.

title: Heart Function Changes During Environmentally Relevant Combined Exposure to Heat, Ultrafine Carbon Black, and Ozone: Role of NOD-like Receptor X1
creator: Chiara Monge, Yulu Li, William Travis Goldsmith, Atefeh Razazan, Murugesan Velayutham, Ethan Meadows, Mark Eminhizer, John M. Hollander, Salik Hussain
description: Highlights What are the main findings? Deletion of NOD-like receptor X1 (NLRX1) impairs the heart’s ability to adapt physiologically after heat exposure. Combined heat and air pollution exposure results in greater lung inflammation compared to individual exposures.NLRX1 deficiency exacerbates lung inflammation and worsens cardiac dysfunction and dyssynchrony during simultaneous extreme heat and air pollution exposure.

title: Ultrasound-Guided Low-Level He-Ne Laser Therapy Following Acupotomy Release for Carpal Tunnel Syndrome: A Multicenter Retrospective Study
creator: Xiang Shang, Guo-Rui Luan, De-Hong Meng, Fen Zhang, San-Bing Wu, Hou-Shan Fang, Fei Li, Yong-Hui Yang
description: BackgroundCarpal tunnel syndrome (CTS) is a common compressive neuropathy associated with pain, sensory disturbance, and functional impairment. Although corticosteroid injection is widely used as an adjunctive treatment for minimally invasive decompression, steroid-related adverse effects limit its clinical application in some patients.

title: Multifunctional Hybrid Nanomedicines for Neurodegenerative Diseases: A Paradigm Shift from Rational Design to Clinical Translation
creator: Yuqin Wu, Mukun Wang, Tianpeng Li, Zhihui Huang, Min Wu, Tingting Sun, Hailin Cong
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Effective drug delivery to the central nervous system remains a persistent challenge owing to the blood–brain barrier (BBB), heterogeneous pathological microenvironments, and the limited capacity of conventional carriers to achieve precise spatiotemporal control over drug release. Multifunctional hybrid nanomedicines (MHNs), defined here as engineered nanosystems that integrate two or more functional modules, such as targeted delivery, controlled release, and/or theranostic capabilities within a single platform, offer a transformative approach to neurotherapeutic design.

title: Non-Radiographic Axial Spondyloarthritis Presenting with Anterior Chest Wall Pain without Inflammatory Back Pain in an HLA-B27–Negative Young Man: A Case Report Highlighting Diagnostic Challenges
creator: Roddy Gergeus, Ahmad Bishr Nasra, Rawia Barghouth, Dalaa Sheikh Ali
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundNon-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis (nr-axSpA) may present with heterogeneous and misleading clinical features, particularly when inflammatory back pain is absent and HLA-B27 is negative. Such presentations can delay recognition and make classification frameworks difficult to apply in routine diagnosis.Case PresentationWe report a 22-year-old Syrian HLA-B27–negative male who initially presented with mild anterior chest wall pain that was clinically interpreted as mechanical and resolved with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs.

title: The “Dark Side” of Pre-Retirement Work Attachment for Later-Life Mental Health: Mediating Role of Retirement Adjustment and Moderating Role of Social Network
creator: Lecheng Chen, Xiaolei Li, Jialing Fan, Yiru Yang
description: BackgroundWith rapid population aging and extended post-retirement lifespan, understanding the modifiable psychological and social processes that shape retirees’ mental health has become increasingly important for behavioral health management. However, the mechanisms linking pre-retirement work attachment and retirement adjustment to post-retirement mental health remain poorly understood.

title: Successful Conversion Surgery after S-1 plus oxaliplatin Plus Zolbetuximab for Initially Unresectable Gastric Cancer with Pancreatic Invasion: A Case Report
creator: Yuma Fuse, Hidetaka Andrew Ono, Masanori Eguchi, Akiko Tamura, Seichiro Shirakabe, Ryo Fujiwara, Yusuke Yoshikawa, Naohiko Sugimura, Yukari Takata, Naoki Maeda, Mayu Kitamoto, Shohei Maruta, Susumu Daibo, Yohei Ota, Hirokazu Suwa, Kenichi Yoshida, Mayumi Yakeishi, Kazunori Nojiri, Takafumi Kumamoto
description: INTRODUCTIONZolbetuximab, a monoclonal antibody targeting claudin 18.2 (CLDN18.2), has recently demonstrated significant survival benefits when combined with chemotherapy for advanced gastric cancer. However, evidence regarding conversion surgery following SOX plus zolbetuximab therapy remains extremely limited.CASE PRESENTATIONA 59-year-old woman presented with epigastric discomfort. Endoscopy revealed a depressed lesion in the lower gastric body, and biopsy confirmed signet-ring cell carcinoma.

title: Predictive Performance of a Serum sRAGE/sVEGFR-3 Dual-Biomarker Combination for Hypercoagulability Status in Pediatric Mycoplasma pneumoniae Pneumonia: A Retrospective Cohort Analysis
creator: Chunzhe Guo, Fang Cheng, Shixin Sun, Lina Kang, Gaoyin Zhang, Hong An
description: ObjectiveTo evaluate serum soluble receptor for advanced glycation end products (sRAGE) and soluble vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 3 (sVEGFR-3) as biomarkers for hypercoagulable state in children with Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (MPP).MethodsWe retrospectively enrolled 352 children with MPP (hypercoagulable, n=98; non-hypercoagulable, n=254). Serum sRAGE and sVEGFR-3 were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA).

title: Complete Skin Clearance is Associated with HADS-Defined Absence of Anxiety and Depressive Symptoms After IL-17A Inhibitor Treatment in Moderate-to-Severe Psoriasis: Evidence from the SPEECH Cohort
creator: Zhenquan Xuan, Yingbao Zhen, Didaer Muheyati, Dawei Huang, Lian Cui, Zeyu Chen, Min Dai, Yuxiong Jiang, Yangfeng Ding, Qian Yu, Yuling Shi
description: BackgroundPsoriasis is a chronic immune-mediated disease associated with anxiety, depressive symptoms, and impaired quality of life, potentially involving interacting psychosocial and inflammatory pathways. During biologic treatment, psychological symptoms may improve alongside skin disease, but whether complete skin clearance (CSC) is associated with Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS)-defined absence of anxiety and depressive symptoms remains unclear.

title: Self-Fitting Versus Professional-Fitting Hearing Aids: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
creator: Ebraheem Albazee, Hajar Alismail, Noof Albannai, Yaqoub Yousef Alenezi, Abdullah M. Alharran, Maya Yassir H. Ibrahim, Durar Ahmed Aljishi, Ahmed Abu-Zaid
description: Background: Adult hearing loss is common, yet hearing-aid uptake remains inadequate due to systemic and financial barriers in traditional audiologist-based fitting models. Over-the-counter (OTC) and self-fitting strategies have emerged to improve accessibility, allowing users to select and adjust their devices independently. However, concerns remain that reducing professional involvement may compromise electroacoustic accuracy, speech-in-noise outcomes, and overall patient satisfaction.

title: Melatonin potentiates the antineoplastic effects of venetoclax in acute myeloid leukemia cells
creator: Vahid Vahedian, Keli Lima, Bruna Oliveira de Almeida, Rita de Cássia Cavaglieri, João Agostinho Machado-Neto, Eduardo Magalhães Rego
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). e disease predominantly affects older adults and remains associated with poor clinical outcomes, particularly in patients who are unfit for intensive chemotherapy due to comorbidities and adverse-risk disease biology [2]. Despite standard myelosuppressive chemotherapy approaches, including anthracycline-cytarabine-based induction and consolidation with or without allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, relapse rates remain high, largely due to the persistence of therapy-resistant leukemic stem cells or clonal evolution or both [3].

title: Anxiety and Depressive Symptoms Among Early‐Year Medical Students in Pakistan: Prevalence, Associated Factors, and Mental Health Service Implications—A Multicenter Cross‐Sectional Study
creator: Farah Rashid, Iffat Noor, Wajeha Najeeb, Hadiya Rashed Siddiqui, Hafiz Muhammad Ali, Abid Malik, Atif Rahman
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAnxiety and depressive symptoms are common among medical students, but multicenter evidence from the early years of training in Pakistan is limited. We estimated symptom prevalence and examined sociodemographic, behavioral, academic, and psychosocial correlates of symptom severity.MethodsWe conducted a multicenter cross‐sectional survey from January to June 2024 among 1630 of 1800 invited first‐ and second‐year students at 9 medical colleges in Islamabad (response rate, 90.6%). Symptoms were assessed with the Patient Health Questionnaire‐9 (PHQ‐9) and Generalized Anxiety Disorder‐7 (GAD‐7).

title: Cutaneous Mast Cell Tumor With Metastasis in a Pet Cairo Spiny Mouse (Acomys cahirinus): A Case Report With Clinicopathologic Characterization
creator: Stephanie E Anderson, Amanda Smith, Shanna R Nelson, Keiichi Kuroki, Chidozie Egbu
description: A 3‐year‐old male pet Cario spiny mouse (Acomys cahirinus) presented with an exophytic, sessile dermal mass at the base of the left ear. Histopathological examination of the excisional biopsy revealed a poorly demarcated, densely cellular neoplasm composed of sheets of round to polygonal cells containing variably distinct basophilic to amphophilic fine intracytoplasmic granules.

title: Metastasis of Pancreatic Intraductal Oncocytic Papillary Neoplasm to the Ovaries
creator: Emily Fronk, Jamie McDowell, Natalia Yanchenko, Hani Katerji, Ashlee Smith, Marcel C C Machado
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectivesIntraductal oncocytic papillary neoplasm (IOPN) is a digestive system tumor typically found in the head of the pancreas. Most often, they remain confined to the pancreas; it is rare that they develop into an invasive carcinoma or metastasize.MethodsThis paper presents the case of a 63‐year‐old postmenopausal female with a past medical history notable for BRCA1 mutation and exploratory laparotomy with pancreatoduodenectomy who underwent risk‐reducing laparoscopic bilateral salpingo‐oophorectomy.ResultsPostoperative pathology revealed metastatic oncocytic papillary neoplasm involving the bilateral ovaries.

title: XIST Is a Key Modulator Associated With the Adhesome Network
creator: Dongning Chen, Nolan Origer, Sha Sun, Timothy L. Downing
description: A long non‐coding RNA (lncRNA) known as the X‐inactivation specific transcript (XIST) plays a central role in X chromosome inactivation—a transcriptional process that silences one of the two X chromosomes in females to ensure dosage compensation between males and females.

title: Real-world use of bempedoic acid for hypercholesterolaemia: a German multicentre, retrospective, cohort study
creator: Linus Haberbosch, Andrea Baessler, Ulrike de Ruiter, David Sinning, Julius L Katzmann, Stephanie Könemann, Ulrike Schatz, Knut Mai, Ursula Kassner, Thomas Bobbert
description: BackgroundDyslipidaemia remains a leading cause of death in Germany despite an improving therapeutic landscape, with many patients not achieving guideline-recommended low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) goals. Bempedoic acid, an adenosine triphosphate citrate lyase inhibitor, is a recent addition to the therapeutic landscape with proven efficacy in randomised controlled trials; however, its use varies between centres.

title: Structural characteristics of local cortical networks wired by distance dependent connectivity rules
creator: Bernhard Hellwig
description: BackgroundThe function of the cerebral cortex is shaped by its anatomical connectivity, yet experimental findings on connection probabilities in local cortical networks remain inconsistent. This study explores structural characteristics of local cortical networks based on distance dependent, Gaussian connectivity profiles. Monolayers of 101 × 101 pyramidal neurons were examined. Their connectivity was based on experimental anatomical or electrophysiological data.

title: Beyond ER-Golgi trafficking: unconventional protein secretion as a new design frontier for synthetic secretion switches in mammalian cells
creator: Bingshun Shi, Xinyuan Qiu, Yongheng Jiang, Jiabo Cai, Lingyun Zhu
description: Mammalian gene switches enable programmable cell behavior. However, current switches on transcriptional and translational layers require de novo RNA and protein synthesis, and secreted outputs must additionally undergo folding, post-translational processing, and intracellular trafficking, imposing delays that limit rapid extracellular responses. Rapid secretion-control switches instead act on pre-synthesized proteins by controlling retention, trafficking, storage, or release.

title: Are we back to normal? Evaluating the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on referrals to a child protection service in a tertiary care centre in Vienna, Austria
creator: Chryssa Grylli, Sophie Klomfar, Johanna Brandlechner, Laura Schaller, Katharina Weimann, Anastasia Pantazidou, Eva Mora-Theuer, Christoph Krall, Catherine Quantin, Susanne Greber-Platzer
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundReports worldwide on suspected child maltreatment (CM) during and after the COVID-19 pandemic have been inconsistent. As no study has yet systematically examined whether structural disruptions to child protection systems have left measurable and lasting traces in referral patterns beyond the acute crisis phase, this study investigated the pandemic’s impact on suspected CM referrals to the Forensic Examination Center for Children and Adolescents (FOKUS) in Vienna, Austria, and whether enduring shifts in CM presentation and referral dynamics have occurred.MethodsRetrospective study using patient

title: Campylobacter jejuni as a Rare Pathogen in CIED Pocket Infections: A Case Report and Literature Review
creator: Karolina Barańska-Pawełczak, Bettina Ziaja, Mariusz Opara, Wojciech Jacheć
description: Patient: Male, 74-year-old Final Diagnosis Campylobacter jejuni infection Symptoms: Swelling of the pacemaker pocket Clinical Procedure: — Specialty: Cardiology Objective: Rare disease BackgroundCardiac implantable electronic device (CIED) infections are usually caused by gram-positive bacteria, whereas gram-negative pathogens are uncommon.Case ReportWe report a case of pacemaker pocket infection caused by Campylobacter jejuni in an immunocompromised patient.

title: Ancestral Sequences Cannot be Accurately Reconstructed via Interpolation in a Variational Autoencoder’s Latent Space
creator: Evan Gorstein, Mengze Tang, Hailey Bruzzone, Claudia Solís-Lemus
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Standard methods for ancestral sequence reconstruction (ASR) rely on substitution models for the residues in a biological sequence and assume independent evolution across these sites, ignoring the epistatic interactions that shape molecular evolution. In contrast, deep learning models like variational autoencoders (VAEs) can learn low-dimensional representations (“embeddings") of sequences in a protein family that may implicitly handle these dependencies, raising the possibility of performing more accurate ASR by interpolating between extant sequence embeddings within the VAE’s latent space.

title: TAPESTRY study: impact of prior transurethral resection of the prostate on outcomes after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy: a propensity score-matched cohort study
creator: Sebastian Lenart, Julia Zach, Georg Gutjahr, Lukas Oberhammer, Stephan Madersbacher, Anton Ponholzer, Clemens Mikulits, Andreas Banner
description: Prior transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) may distort bladder neck and apical anatomy and complicate robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP). Its effect on anastomotic recovery and oncological control remains controversial. To evaluate perioperative, anastomotic, pathological, and available PSA outcomes after RARP in patients with and without prior TURP.

title: Integrating optimal patient-centered care: patient- and family-reported experiences after complex treatment for rare diseases
creator: Frederiek L. Tijssens, Philippine Kies, Lissy de Ridder, Anne P. J. de Pagter, Jeanine M. M. van Klink
description: BackgroundAlthough life expectancy after complex treatments for rare diseases during childhood has increased, long-term medical, psychosocial and societal impacts remain for children and their families. Evaluating patient and family experiences is essential for the development and optimization of integrated patient-centered, value-based care pathways.

title: Tangier Disease
creator: Sabitha Sasidharan Pillai, Preneet Cheema Brar, Ambika P Ashraf
description: Purpose of ReviewWe describe two patients with Tangier disease (TD) and provide a narrative review of its clinical features, genetics, diagnosis, and management. A literature search of PubMed and Google Scholar was performed to identify English-language publications on TD, and relevant articles were reviewed narratively.

title: Central gland detachment following prostate artery embolization: incidence, risk factors and clinical outcomes
creator: Fergus O’Herlihy, Sean Collins, Matthew Laffey, Kiaran O’Malley, Richard E. Power, Cormac Farrelly
description: BackgroundCentral gland detachment (CGD) is a potential complication following prostate artery embolisation (PAE). There is limited information regarding its incidence, associated risk factors, and voiding and ejaculatory function after CGD.MethodsSixty-five consecutive patients undergoing PAE in a single institution were included in this retrospective cohort study. Baseline demographics, radiologic, procedural and clinical outcome data were gathered for all patients.

title: An Exploratory Accounting Approach for Balancing Environmental Impacts of Point and Diffuse Sources in Nitrogen Trading
creator: Jing Lu, Katherine R. O’Brien, Felix Egger, Tony Weber, Jon M. Olley, Matthew P. Adams, Michele A. Burford
description: Nutrient trading between point and diffuse sources of nutrients offers an integrated watershed nutrient management approach to achieve nutrient reduction goals that benefit both the terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems. This market-based approach requires quantification of the environmental impacts of nutrients derived from different sources. This environmental impact depends on the forms, concentrations, loads, transport, and processing of nutrients within waterways.

title: Explaining symptoms in general practice: a predictive processing framework for primary care consultations
creator: Kees van Boven, Peter Lucassen, Tim Olde Hartman, Omer Van den Bergh
description: AimsTo present predictive processing as a clinically useful framework for explaining symptom variability in general practice consultations.MethodsDevelopment of a conceptual framework through an iterative process of theoretical synthesis and clinical translation, informed by a supporting literature search integrating literature on predictive processing and symptom perception with primary care literature on consultation practice and persistent physical symptoms.

title: How does a national blood operator detect early infectious disease signals affecting blood and cellular therapy product safety and sufficiency?
creator: Leisa Bruneau, Carmen L Charlton, Sandra Ramirez‐Arcos, Dilini Kumaran, David Allan, Olivia Norman, Matthew Seftel, Evan M Bloch, Chantale Pambrun, Sheila F O'Brien, Cynthia Cranney, Steven J Drews
description: BackgroundPublic access to up‐to‐date information on infectious diseases and outbreaks has grown rapidly with the advent of artificial intelligence platforms. While this information can improve patient care and support research, the sheer volume of available data coupled with the challenge of identifying misinformation and disinformation can be overwhelming.

title: Fungal extracellular vesicles reshape Lactobacillus rhamnosus vesicles to enhance lysosomal homeostasis and resolve intestinal inflammation
creator: Zhengmei Ji, Guoliang Chen, Xiaolong He, Xiangqian Zhang, Bin Chen, Hang Xiao, Yurong Guo, Yanhui Han
description: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are emerging mediators of intercellular and interkingdom communication. While bacterial EVs directly modulate host health, whether exogenous vesicles can reprogram gut microbial vesiculation and bioactivity remains unclear. Using a defined in vitro conditioning system, ScEV exposure altered EV production by Lactobacillus rhamnosus, generating ScEV-conditioned L. rhamnosus vesicles (ScEV-LrEVs).

title: Impact of Concomitant Grade I Degenerative Spondylolisthesis on Clinical and Radiographic Outcomes
creator: Hinpetch Daungsupawong, Viroj Wiwanitkit
description: ficant issue, as degenerative spondylolisthesis grade I often complicates the decision-making process for decompression in patients with lumbar spinal stenosis. Analysis found that the presence of DS1 did not significantly alter 12-month clinical outcomes between biportal endoscopic laminectomy and microscopic laminectomy.

title: Cognitive Function Influences Longitudinal Motor Function Recovery after Proximal Femoral Fracture: A Longitudinal Analysis
creator: Takehiro Kaneoka, Tomohiro Kawazoe, Kazuhiro Yamazaki, Gen Shiraishi, Takashi Sakai
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Objectives:As the incidence of proximal femoral fractures (PFFs) continues to increase, optimizing patient-specific treatment strategies is essential for the efficient use of healthcare resources. The aim of this study was to examine longitudinal postoperative motor function recovery in patients with femoral neck fractures (FNF) and intertrochanteric fractures (ITFs) and to identify which factors, including fracture type and patient-related characteristics, predominantly influence recovery trajectories to inform individualized rehabilitation strategies.Methods:This retrospective study included patients who underwent bipolar hip arthroplasty for FNF (201 hips) or

title: Your voice matters: using participatory film to engage people with chronic pain in public involvement and research
creator: Sarah A. Harrisson, Samina Begum, Claire Toussaint, Mark Agathangelou, James Rattee, Melanie A. Holden, Krysia Canvin
description: BackgroundPeople living with chronic pain (≥ 3-months) often struggle to participate in valued activity (for example, family life, work and in their community) and are under-represented in public involvement and research. We aimed to broaden awareness and encourage engagement in public involvement and research among people living with chronic pain.

title: Standardizing Rectal Suction Biopsy Preparation With a Dedicated Equipment Box: A Quality Improvement Project
creator: Yasir Alkhatib
description: Rectal suction biopsy is an established diagnostic procedure for suspected Hirschsprung disease, but reliable performance depends on having multiple pieces of equipment, consumables, specimen containers, and documentation immediately available. In our paediatric surgical clinical area, the required items were stored in different locations, resulting in avoidable searching, workflow interruptions, and the possibility of missing essential equipment during preparation.

title: Patient-Reported Outcomes Following Two-Tined Three-Site Conventional Radiofrequency Ablation of Genicular Nerves for Chronic Knee Pain
creator: Mingda Chen, Sercan Tosun, Nicolas R Thompson, Kush Goyal
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background: Genicular nerve radiofrequency ablation (GNRFA) has emerged as an effective therapy for chronic knee pain. Although some studies have evaluated its effectiveness, there is limited real-world data on the long-term patient-reported outcome (PRO) data for GNRFAs.Objective: This study aimed to evaluate PROs following conventional GNRFAs performed using two-tined electrodes and the classical three-site technique targeting the superior medial, superior lateral, and inferior medial genicular nerves.Methods: We performed a retrospective chart review to gather data from consecutive GNRFAs at an academic medical

title: Imaging nanoscopic co-assemblies of α-synuclein and Tau in human samples
creator: Yu P Zhang, Amber Wallis, Clara Obensa Bertroli, Cherida Zhang, Melanie Burke, Florence Layburn, Evgeniia Lobanova, Martin Furlepa, Shekhar Kedia, Yuhao Cui, Prasanna Suresh, Woo Suk Yang, Annelies Quaegebeur, Tim Bartels, Caroline H Williams-Gray, David Klenerman
description: α-synuclein (αS), amyloid-β (Aβ), and Tau aggregates are hallmarks of many neurodegenerative diseases, yet the prevalence and nature of their nanoscopic co-assemblies remain poorly understood. Here, we adapt a single-molecule pull-down (SiMPull) assay to profile αS, Aβ, and Tau co-assemblies across post-mortem brain tissue homogenates, soluble brain fractions, human serum, cerebrospinal fluid, and saliva.

title: Comparability of food frequency questionnaires between Korean Children’s Environmental Health Study (Ko-CHENS) and Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study (KoGES) in pregnant women
creator: Minsu Cho, Bom Kim, Hyesook Kim, Sunghun Na, Se Jin Lee, Tae Gyu Ahn, Kyung Ho Son, Woo Jin Kim, Jung Eun Lee, Ko-CHENS Study Group
description: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVESThe Korean Children’s Environmental Health Study (Ko-CHENS) developed a food frequency questionnaire (FFQ) to assess maternal dietary intake during pregnancy. This FFQ shares high structural similarity with the validated FFQ of the Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study (KoGES), a representative dietary assessment tool for the Korean adult population, which includes 97 of the 112 items in the Ko-CHENS FFQ.

title: Structural alterations in the superior temporal gyrus associated with depressive symptoms in migraine without aura: a voxel-based morphometry and surface-based morphometry magnetic resonance imaging study
creator: Donghai Chen, Yayin Luo, Yuhao Zhang, Wenlong Zhang, Zhuqing Yuan, Zhixuan He, Haochong Xie, Meijun Qu, Tong Lin, Jiawei Li, Qingwei Song, Yanwei Miao, Zhe Wang, Jian Jiang, Renwang Pu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundMigraine without aura (MwoA) frequently co-occurs with depressive symptoms, yet the neurobiological mechanisms underlying this comorbidity remain insufficiently characterized. This study integrated voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and surface-based morphometry (SBM) to compare gray matter volume (GMV) and cortical morphology between patients with MwoA and healthy controls (HC) and to further determine whether structural brain alterations vary across MwoA subgroups stratified by depressive symptom severity, thereby identifying potential structural correlates of depressive symptoms in this population.MethodsA total of 67 patients with MwoA {38 with

title: Genetic diversity and morphology of South Korean Aedes koreicus (Diptera: Culicidae) provide insights into the origin of European populations
creator: Junyoung Lee, Jungyoon Lee, Changseob Lim, Ji Hyoun Kang, Sangwoo Seok, Hee Il Lee, Yeon Jae Bae
description: BackgroundAedes koreicus (Edwards, 1917) is native to Korea, northern China, and the Russian Far East, and has gained attention following its first detection in Europe in 2008 and subsequent spread across Europe. The Korean Peninsula, which includes the type locality of Ae.

title: Low-dose, high-frequency simulation with respiratory function monitor feedback enhances face mask ventilation across neonatal resuscitation devices: A prospective study in neonatology fellows
creator: Samantha J Carlton, Joseph L Hagan, Nicole K Neveln, Daniel S Lemke, Nathan C Sundgren
description: Face mask ventilation (FMV) is a critical skill in neonatal resuscitation, yet structured assessment of neonatology fellow competence has remained limited. This study evaluated whether low-dose, high-frequency simulation with real-time respiratory function monitor (RFM) feedback improved FMV performance across commonly used ventilation devices.

title: A telomere-to-telomere assembly of the white mulberry (Morus alba) genome provides insights into karyotype evolution and the white-fruit phenotype in Morus
creator: Fangfang Peng, Xunlan Li, Zhaoxin Wei, Guohui Han, Xiaoyu Wang
description: r n = 14 [2]. To date, telomere-to-telomere (T2T) genomes have been reported for the wild species Morus notabilis (n = 7) [3] and Morus mongolica (n = 14) [4]. However, white mulberry (M. alba), the most widely cultivated species within the n = 14 group, lacks a complete T2T reference genome. Such a resource would address two major limitations.

title: TrenibotulinumtoxinE: Pharmacology, clinical evidence, and emerging role in aesthetic medicine
creator: Chaocheng Liu, Jean Carruthers, Alain Michon
description: SummaryBotulinum neurotoxin type A (BoNT/A) products are among the most popular aesthetic treatments worldwide, but their relatively prolonged duration may be a barrier for patients who are concerned about unnatural appearance, adverse effects, or being committed to an unwanted result.

title: Prescribing for the patient and the planet: a pragmatic feasibility study of a behaviour change intervention to reduce liquid amoxicillin prescribing in primary care
creator: Adam Pattison Rathbone, Joseph Pickles, Ms Laura Griffiths, Alice McCloskey, Philippa McCabe, Nicola Vasey, Emma Lim
description: BackgroundOral liquid medicines can be clinically appropriate but may be used when solid oral formulations are feasible, with implications for medicine costs and environmental sustainability. We evaluated the feasibility of GPILL, a theory-informed intervention using prescribing feedback, social norms and information on formulation-associated carbon dioxide equivalent (CO₂e) emissions to support reduced liquid amoxicillin prescribing in primary care.

title: A systematic review of intracranial atherosclerosis epidemiology—the largest contributor to the global ischemic stroke burden?
creator: Davor Pavlin-Premrl, Vincent Thijs, Peter J. Mitchell, Nawaf Yassi, Mark Parsons, Anna H. Balabanski, Julian Maingard, Hamed Asadi, Ashu Jhamb, Ali Khabaza, Adam Zheng, Aaron Gaekwad, Catherine Voutier, Bruce CV. Campbell
description: BackgroundIntracranial atherosclerosis (ICAD) is commonly stated to be the largest contributor to the ischemic stroke burden worldwide. However, there has been little systematic examination of the epidemiology literature.MethodsPubMed, OVID-EMBASE and manual searches of references from retrieved literature were used to identify studies. Adult studies from 1990 onwards were included, with two reviewers independently reviewing titles and abstracts.

title: Exploring the effects of digital literacy training on college students’ self-leadership: a longitudinal randomized controlled trial
creator: Kefei Tan
description: ObjectiveSelf-leadership is recognized as a critical self-regulatory capacity for academic success and personal development. While prior correlational studies have linked digital literacy to self-regulated learning, experimental evidence for a potential directional pathway from digital literacy enhancement to self-leadership development remains scarce.

title: Primary cutaneous adenoid cystic carcinoma arising in the axilla: a case report and literature review
creator: Si Li, Fang Yang, Yangyang Jiang, Shuanghai Hu
description: Primary cutaneous adenoid cystic carcinoma (PCACC) is a rare cutaneous adnexal malignancy. Although its clinical course is generally considered more indolent than that of salivary gland-derived counterparts, PCACC exhibits a significant propensity for local recurrence and a notable potential for distant metastasis. Here, we report a rare case of PCACC arising in the right axilla.

title: Spatial multi-omics-guided drug development in inflammatory bowel disease: from mucosal immune niches to precision therapy
creator: Hai Wang, Xiaolong Zhao, Jie Yang
description: Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis are now treated with an expanding set of biologics and small molecules, yet treatment selection remains largely empirical. Primary non-response, secondary loss of response, incomplete mucosal healing, fibrostenosis, and fistulizing disease show that conventional clinical, endoscopic, and bulk molecular markers do not capture how disease is organized within tissue.

title: Early time-of-day infusion of PD-1 inhibitor improves prognosis in advanced gastric cancer: a multicenter real-world study
creator: Ziting Qu, Xiaoyu Guo, Shupei Zhang, Yanyan Zhao, Zhenyan Hu, Wenxi Ding, Sachiyo Nomura, Yiyin Zhang, Xiaoli Wei
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundWhether the time-of-day administration (ToDA) of programmed cell death 1 (PD-1) inhibitor infusion influences survival in advanced gastric cancer (AGC) remains unclear. This research aimed to evaluate the impact of ToDA on the prognosis of AGC patients.MethodsThis multicenter retrospective study enrolled 416 AGC patients receiving PD-1 inhibitor therapy, who were divided into early and late ToDA groups based on sensitivity analyses using 30-minute intervals of the administration time window.

title: Editorial: Case reports in veterinary neurology and neurosurgery, volume II
creator: Koen M. Santifort, Joao Miguel De Frias, Simone Spinillo, Bruno A. Lopes, Susana Monforte Monteiro
description: nge of subjects, including clinical phenomena, histopathological diagnoses, genetic disorders, and other. In this second volume (Case Reports in Veterinary Neurology and Neurosurgery, Volume II), no less than 24 articles are included. Of these, nine pertain to cats, one to foxes, and 14 to dogs.

title: Ozoralizumab, a trivalent anti-TNFα NANOBODY® compound, is resistant to rheumatoid factor-mediated modulation of FcRn-dependent recycling and immune complex uptake
creator: Mai Morimoto, Yukihisa Sawa, Chihiro Ishiwatari-Ogata, Naoki Kojima, Yasuyuki Fujii
description: Rheumatoid factor (RF), an autoantibody targeting IgG, is a key diagnostic marker of autoimmune diseases, especially rheumatoid arthritis (RA). In patients with RA, high RF titers have been reported to be associated with disease severity and may influence the pharmacological behavior and clinical response of certain biologic agents, including tumor necrosis factor (TNF) inhibitors.

title: Sepsis-associated thrombotic microangiopathy–like syndrome following cardiac surgery: a case report
creator: Chujun Yang, Shanshan Dong, Zhijing Xia, Wan Peng, Hua Yan, Zhenlu Zhang, Qimei Wei
description: Severe sepsis following cardiac surgery may be accompanied by a thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA)-like syndrome distinct from classic immune-mediated thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP) and overt disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC). We report a 62-year-old man who developed sepsis after mitral valve replacement, complicated by thrombocytopenia (nadir 45 × 10⁹/L), microangiopathic hemolysis (2.6% schistocytes), and multiple organ dysfunction.

title: Role of the ketogenic diet in neurodevelopmental disorders: neuroprotection and clinical practice
creator: Luqiang Sun, Liu Qu, Shuqing Gao, Juan Chen, Pan Wu, Haichuan Wang
description: Neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs), such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), occur early in life and affect cognitive and behavioral health and motor development. While hereditary factors contribute to the development of ASD, recent research has shown that environmental factors, notably nutritional factors, play important roles in determining the severity and expression of symptoms.

title: Onco-anxiology: a proposal for an anxiety-focused, longitudinal framework within cancer care
creator: Chirag Jain
